model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, and MEMIT, with the additional method ROMEO. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^0$ to $10^4$, with labeled ticks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale from 40 to 65, with major gridlines and labels at intervals of 5. The data for each method is represented by a distinct line: Base (black, solid line with circles), FT (blue, dashed line with triangles), IKE (red, solid line with triangles), MEND (brown, dashed line with diamonds), and MEMIT (purple, dashed line with diamonds). The ROMEO method is represented by a green, solid line with squares. The plot shows that the accuracy of all methods generally increases as the co-occurrence number increases. The ROMEO method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, starting at approximately 51% and rising to over 65%. The MEND and MEMIT methods show similar trends, with MEND starting at around 44% and ending at about 56%, and MEMIT starting at 43% and ending at 55%. The FT method starts at about 40% and increases to approximately 47%. The Base method shows the lowest accuracy, starting at around 39% and ending at 44%.
